Thanks again for the demo this morning — helpful session. A quick recap from our side and a few follow-up questions to help with sizing and pricing: 

Summary of current signal:
- Product: PayAssist (customer support assistant) built on Llama 2-70B (we run an internal quantized variant)
- Expected steady-state tokens: ~1.8B tokens / month (includes prompts + responses)
- Peak concurrency: ~100 concurrent sessions during support spikes
- Average request: 350 tokens in, ~120 tokens out
- Sequence length: often 4096 context; some >4096 for longer threads

Requirements / asks:
1) We want a dedicated/reserved capacity arrangement (monthly commit) — target: predictability and data isolation
2) GPU preference: our infra team prefers H100 for throughput, but A100 80GB is OK if unit economics are significantly better
3) Throughput target: should sustain peak without falling back to hosted; target ~120 concurrent with 300–400 tokens/sec aggregate (low-latency important)
4) Budget: internal procurement is looking for target economics in the range of $150–$250 per 1M tokens (we know exact price depends on batching/efficiency)

Next steps from PayWise: can you provide a short sizing and pricing note that shows: recommended GPU type, reserved GPU count, expected tokens/sec per GPU (assumptions on batching/kv cache), and ballpark $/1M tokens + committed monthly cost? I can attach a short usage CSV (sending separately) with hourly ramp over last 30 days to help sizing.

Thanks — Alicia

Internal -> public reply included below. Draft sizing + pricing notes (high level) — attaching a 1-pager (redwood-dedicated-sizing-v1.pdf).

Assumptions from call / CSV (preliminary):
- Model: Llama 2-70B q4_8 or q5_0 variant (your quantized runtime)
- Typical context: mixed; assume 60% requests <= 4096, 40% > 4096 (occasionally up to 8192)
- Average tokens per request: 470 (in+out)
- Hourly peak concurrency: 100 sessions -> estimate peak tokens/sec demand ~ 8k–12k tokens/sec across the pool (depends on tail behavior)

GPU recommendation:
- Primary: H100 80GB (preferred) — better throughput for 70B, better fp16 kernel performance, and gives headroom for larger contexts
- Fallback: A100 80GB if procurement/cost requires it — expect ~15–25% lower throughput vs H100 for this workload

Sizing guidance (reserved pool):
- Start: 4 x H100 80GB reserved nodes (with autoscale burst to additional nodes if needed)
  - Expected steady throughput (with continuous batching + prefix KV cache): ~2.0–3.5k tokens/sec per GPU for mixed context; peak-per-GPU could be ~4–5k tokens/sec with aggressive batching
  - So 4 GPUs -> baseline 8k–14k tokens/sec aggregate (matches your peak target)
- If you need lower p99 latency under burst load, 6 x H100 recommended (adds headroom and reduces landing-tolerance to <200ms p95 with conservative batching)

Estimated unit economics (ballpark, committed monthly pricing on Dedicated):
- 4 x H100 reserved: estimated $/1M tokens = $140–$200 (depends on sustained batch efficiency and cache hit rate)
- 6 x H100 reserved: estimated $/1M tokens = $110–$160 (better amortization of fixed infra costs)
- A100 variants typically shift the range +10–20% (i.e., higher $/1M) due to lower throughput for 70B workloads

Example committed monthly cost (very rough):
- 4 x H100 reserved: ~$36k–$52k / month (depending on support & extra features)
- 6 x H100 reserved: ~$52k–$78k / month

Notes / levers to optimize:
- Quantization level (q4_8 vs q5_0) — more aggressive quant reduces memory and improves throughput, lowering $/1M
- Prefix/KV caching — if a large fraction of requests share prefixes, effective tokens served from model drop sharply
- Batching policy — we can tune to hit budget vs latency targets; we’ll present 2–3 tradeoff configs in the follow-up doc

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-v1.pdf (assumptions + sample pricing table)

- Aditya: share the CSV Alicia mentioned (if not already shared) so I can run a quick sizing simulator
- Alicia: confirm whether <4096> is majority or edge case
- We schedule a 30–45m sizing review tomorrow (I’m available 1–4pm PT)
